newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA EXCHANGE SAYS WHEAT FUTURES A POSSIBILITY.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA EXCHANGE SAYS WHEAT FUTURES A POSSIBILITY.

text.p: The South African Futures Exchange (Safex) said on Tuesday that the launch of a wheat futures was "a possibility" but denied a local newspaper report that there were firm plans to launch a contract next year.
"It's a definite possibility but we haven't got any plans or any time frame," Safex agricultural division head John Wixley told Reuters.
At present South Africa's wheat market remains firmly in the hands of the Wheat Board which operates a single channel market.
However, legislation passed in parliament in October will mean the Wheat Board and other statutory agricultural market control boards have to disband by the end of next year.
Safex currently has agricultural futures contracts for yellow and white maize, beef and potatoes.
